edges.description: Reduced enzyme activity decreases conversion of 5-oxo-L-proline to glutamate, causing the substrate to accumulate in body fluids and be excreted in urine.
Accumulated 5-oxo-L-proline is excreted as urinary L-pyroglutamic acid.
Increased urinary 5-oxoproline reports failure of substrate clearance by deficient 5-oxoprolinase.
The biochemical measurement corresponds to the urinary L-pyroglutamic-acid HPO phenotype.
Reduced activity is the direct functional readout of deficient OPLAH molecular function.

nodes.description: Failure to clear 5-oxo-L-proline, also called pyroglutamic acid, causes its accumulation in body fluids and persistent urinary excretion. This is the defining and reproducible biochemical phenotype. No causal edge is drawn from this node to the reported clinical findings because that relationship has not been established.

nodes.description: Molecularly confirmed individuals carry homozygous or compound heterozygous OPLAH variants. Reported alleles include truncating and missense variants, many private to individual families. Functional or segregation evidence is particularly important for missense variants.
